acceptance_criteria: Design-point efficiency reproduced within 1 percentage point; turbine-trip transient runs stably in real time; docs state the paper-design caveat.
description:
600 MWt, 850 degC core outlet (upgraded design 950 degC), NON-INTERCOOLED cycle chosen for simplicity. Baseline 45.6% net efficiency; upgraded design breaks 50%.

Components: recuperator, precooler, compressor, turbine.

THE PIECE THAT IS NOT A SIMPLE SERIES LOOP - RPV COOLING FLOW PATH: compressor outlet helium at ~550 degC from the recuperator flows UPWARD along the RPV inner surface to keep the vessel below the SA533 steel limit. It is a load-dependent bypass stream the in-core structure was designed around. Model it as such.

WHY THIS DESIGN IS WORTH SIMULATING: direct-cycle coupling means no steam generator decouples core from turbine, so a turbine trip propagates STRAIGHT into core flow. That is the interesting transient.

CAVEAT FOR DOCS: GTHTR300 is a PAPER DESIGN with no experimental validation. Validate physics against HTTR; use GTHTR300 only as a plant configuration. Zero GTHTR references exist in the workspace today (verified 2026-08-13).

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
Cross-link from op-id3l.2 (helium fast path), maintainer note 2026-08-13.

(p,s) retains an extra iteration even in CoolProp's TABULAR backends -- and (p,s) is precisely what isentropic turbine and compressor expansion needs in this Brayton cycle. So the ONE place a hand-rolled backward relation for helium is likely to earn its keep is here in the BOP, not in the core.

Everywhere else, (p,h) and (p,T) are the tabular backends' native gridded inputs and are already fast. Do not write bespoke helium backward relations for the core path. -q

title: HTGR Phase 5: GTHTR300 direct helium Brayton balance of plant
